astar.name: A*
astar.blurb: Balances how far you've come against how far you've got left. Finds the shortest path while still aiming at the goal.
astar.affinity: it has the best f = g + h score on the frontier

dijkstra.name: Dijkstra
dijkstra.blurb: Always expands whatever's cheapest to reach, and couldn't care less where the goal is. Finds the shortest path, just spreads out everywhere to do it.
dijkstra.affinity: it is the cheapest cell reached so far, and where the goal sits is not considered

greedy.name: Greedy best-first
greedy.blurb: Always jumps toward whatever looks closest to the goal and ignores how far it's already walked. Fast, but the path it finds might not be the shortest.
greedy.affinity: it looks closest to the goal, and the distance already travelled is ignored

bfs.name: Breadth-first
bfs.blurb: Expands cells in the order it found them, treating every move as equal. Spreads out in neat rings from the start.
bfs.affinity: it has waited on the frontier longest, and every move costs the same

manhattan.label: Manhattan
manhattan.blurb: Counts steps along the grid. That's the real remaining distance here, so A* walks almost straight to the goal.

euclidean.label: Euclidean
euclidean.blurb: Straight-line distance. You can't actually move diagonally, so this underestimates every move — A* hedges and fans out a bit like Dijkstra. Still finds the shortest path though.

euclideanSquared.label: Euclidean squared
euclideanSquared.blurb: Straight-line distance, squared. A big overestimate, so A* charges straight at the goal and barely explores — but it gives up the shortest-path guarantee to do it.

custom.label: Custom
custom.blurb: Your own formula over the x and y distances to the goal.

frontierPanel.title: Frontier
frontierPanel.empty: Nothing on the frontier yet. Press play to start the search.

tooltip.checkingNext: Checking this one next — it is at the top of the queue right now.
tooltip.queuePosition: Currently waiting at position {position} in the queue.
tooltip.scoredByDistance: Scored by how far it still looks:

pullSentence.prefix: The best step from here is

verdict.overpays: That's more than the move actually costs, so f keeps dropping — the search beelines for the goal. The catch: it might give up the shortest-path guarantee to do it.
verdict.exact: Exactly what the step costs, so f stays flat here on the best route — barely any wandering.
verdict.underpays: That's less than the move costs, so f creeps up by {amount} per move from here. Other directions stay in the running too, which is why the search fans out.

tooltip.noFavorite: Every direction looks equally far from the goal right now, so the heuristic has no favorite.
tooltip.noHeuristic: No heuristic here — {algorithmName} doesn't estimate what's left, so nothing looks better than anything else. Every neighbour is equally worth trying.

cellsExpanded.subtitle: The speed axis. Lower is faster.

pathLength.subtitle: The correctness axis. Zero means the shortest path; anything else is a wrong answer.
